# The settings

**98 settings in 13 groups.** Generated by `npm run spec`.

Everything an administrator can change without a deployment. This is also the
answer to *what may differ between two practices*: the standing decision of
3 September 2026 is that a second practice gets a database of its own, and that
anything differing between practices belongs here or in a vocabulary — because
those already live inside the practice’s own database and so become
per-practice for free.

## AI Assistant

Which model the assistant uses. It suggests; a person always presses the button. The register works with all of this switched off.

Owned by `assistant`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ai.model` | enum | `claude-haiku-4-5` | Haiku is the default and is the right one for this work: reading a document into form fields, triaging a message, summarising a file — all of it checked by a person before anything is written. Move up if extraction from difficult scans starts costing you more in corrections than the model saves. |
| `ai.workspace_id` | string | _blank_ | Only needed for an identity-linked key, which refuses any request that does not say which workspace it acts in. It starts with “wrkspc_” and is in the address bar when you open the workspace in the Anthropic Console under Settings → Workspaces. Leave empty for an ordinary key: the header is then not sent at all, which is what an ordinary key expects. |

## Practice

Who you are, as it appears on quotes and outgoing correspondence.

Owned by `admin`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `practice.legal_name` | string | _blank_ | Shown at the top of printed quotes. |
| `practice.contact_email` | string | _blank_ | Where clients should reply. Shown on quotes. |
| `practice.reply_to` | string | _blank_ | Left empty, replies go back to the sending address. Set it when the address the provider is allowed to send from is not a mailbox anybody reads — a provider will only send from a domain verified with it, and that domain may have no mailbox behind it. |
| `practice.acceptance_notify` | string | _blank_ | Where the register sends its note when a client accepts a quotation online. Left empty it goes to the practice email above. Set it to reach somebody else — an assistant, or a shared inbox — without changing the address clients see. |
| `practice.contact_phone` | string | _blank_ | Contact phone |
| `practice.postal_address` | text | _blank_ | Shown on quotes, one line per line. |
| `practice.gst_number` | string | _blank_ | Printed on every quote when set. Leave blank if the practice is not GST registered. |
| `practice.adviser_details` | text | _blank_ | Licence or admission details, as they should appear on a quote. |
| `practice.email_signature` | text | _blank_ | How you sign off an email that leaves the register — name, title, phone, and any confidentiality notice. Paste it in as plain text, exactly as you want a client to read it; blank lines are kept. Left empty, the register signs off with the practice name, email and phone above. Anything the letter already says — a link to the terms of engagement, for instance — is better left out here than said twice. |
| `practice.bank_account_holder` | string | _blank_ | Printed on quotes so a client knows exactly who to pay. |
| `practice.bank_name` | string | _blank_ | Bank |
| `practice.bank_account_number` | string | _blank_ | Shown on quotes only when the box below is ticked. |
| `practice.show_bank_on_quote` | boolean | `false` | Off by default. A quote is often forwarded on, and account details invite the invoice-redirection fraud that is common in professional services. Turn it on only if your terms of engagement expect it. |
| `practice.terms_url` | string | `https://www.immigration.kiwi/terms` | Referenced on every quote. Clients read the terms at this address, so it must be the same one your letter of engagement sends them to. |
| `practice.terms_label` | string | `Barrister’s Terms of Engagement` | How the document is named on the quote. |

## Security

Policy applied to everyone who signs in.

Owned by `auth`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `security.require_two_factor` | boolean | `false` | Anyone without it is sent to set it up before they can use the register. Turn this on once you have set up your own. |
| `security.password_min_length` | integer | `12` | Length does more for a password than composition rules. It cannot be set below 12. |
| `security.trusted_device_days` | integer | `40` | After entering a code, a person can tick "remember this machine". For this many days that machine asks for the password only. The password is always asked for. Counted from the day the code was entered and not extended by use. 0 turns it off and asks every time; 90 is the most allowed. |

The public page at the root of this site, shown to anyone who is not signed in. The list fields take one item per line, written as “Heading \| text”.

Owned by `landing`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `website.enabled` | boolean | `true` | When off, visitors who are not signed in go straight to the sign-in screen. |
| `website.allow_indexing` | boolean | `false` | Off by default: this address also serves the client register. Turn it on only when the page is on a domain you are happy to see in search results. |
| `website.eyebrow` | string | `New Zealand immigration law` | Line above the headline |
| `website.headline` | string | `Immigration advice that holds up.` | Headline |
| `website.lede` | text | `Visas, residence and the applications that have gone wrong — prepared by a barrister who does this and nothing else, for a fee agreed before the work starts.` | Opening paragraph |
| `website.stats` | text | `15+ \| years in immigration law
Fixed \| quoted before work starts
NZ-wide \| onshore and offshore clients` | Figures under the headline |
| `website.services` | text | `Work visas \| Accredited Employer Work Visas, job-change applications and the employer accreditation behind them.
Residence \| Skilled Migrant, partnership and parent category residence, prepared to be decided rather than queried.
Partnership \| Partnership-based work and residence, where the evidence of the relationship is the case.
Student and visitor \| Study pathways, visitor extensions and the timing that keeps someone lawfully here.
When something goes wrong \| Section 61 requests, PPI responses, reconsiderations and appeals to the Tribunal.
A second opinion \| Advice on an application you are preparing yourself, before it is lodged rather than after.` | What you do |
| `website.process` | text | `Talk it through \| A first conversation about what you want and whether it is realistic. You leave knowing where you stand.
A written plan and a fixed quote \| The visa pathway, what it will take, what it will cost. Nothing starts until you accept it.
Preparation \| Documents, evidence and submissions assembled properly, with you told what is needed and by when.
Lodgement and beyond \| Filed, tracked and answered. You hear from us when something changes, not only when it is finished.` | How working together goes |
| `website.about_title` | string | `Who you are dealing with` | About — heading |
| `website.about` | text | `One practice, one person accountable for your file. You are not handed to whoever is free; the person who advises you is the person who prepares the application and the person who answers when you ring.

Immigration decisions turn on evidence and on timing. Most of the work is making sure the case is complete before it is lodged, so that the decision is made on what you sent rather than on what an officer had to ask for.` | About — text |
| `website.faq` | text | `How much will it cost? \| You get a fixed written quote before any work begins, itemised, with GST and any Immigration New Zealand fees shown separately. If the matter changes, so does the quote — in writing, in advance.
How long does it take? \| Preparation is usually a few weeks; the decision is Immigration New Zealand’s and varies by visa. You are told the current processing times for your category at the outset rather than an optimistic guess.
Can you help if I have already been declined? \| Often, yes. A decline is not always the end: depending on the reasons there may be a reconsideration, a section 61 request, an appeal to the Immigration and Protection Tribunal, or a stronger fresh application. This is worth a conversation quickly, because most of these have short deadlines.
Do I have to be in New Zealand? \| No. Most matters are handled by email and video call, and clients are advised offshore as often as onshore.
What happens to my information? \| It is held in this practice’s own register, on servers we control, and it is not sold, shared or used for anything but your matter.` | Questions people ask |
| `website.enquiry_form` | boolean | `false` | Adds a short form that creates an inquiry in the register. Off by default — with it off the page shows your email address instead. |
| `website.seo_title` | string | _blank_ | What appears as the heading in a search result and on the browser tab. Leave blank to use the practice name and the line above the headline. Around 60 characters reads best. |
| `website.canonical_url` | string | _blank_ | The address the public should reach this page on, e.g. https://immigration.kiwi. **Every link sent to a client is built on this** — fee quotes, letters of engagement, document lists — as well as the canonical link, the sitemap and the structured data. Left blank, those links carry whatever address the register was opened on, which in production is its own workers.dev name. Set it only once a domain actually points at the register: an address that does not reach it produces links that do not work. |
| `website.service_area` | string | `New Zealand` | Named in the structured data search engines and AI assistants read. |
| `website.practice_type` | enum | `LegalService` | The schema.org type published in the structured data. |
| `website.closing` | text | `Tell us what you are trying to do and where you have got to. You will get a straight answer about whether it is worth pursuing.` | Closing invitation |

## Decisions and chasing INZ

When a decision is expected after lodgement, and what happens when that date passes.

Owned by `cases`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cases.expected_decision_months` | integer | `1` | Filled in automatically when a matter is lodged without an expected decision date. Always editable on the matter itself — this is a starting point, not a rule. |
| `cases.chase_enabled` | boolean | `true` | Assigned to whoever owns the matter. Turn it off for one matter on the matter itself. |
| `cases.chase_schedule` | string | `0, 1, 2` | Counted from the expected decision date, so 0 chases on the day it was expected. With a one-month expectation, “0, 1, 2” chases one, two and three months after lodgement. Up to twelve, separated by commas. |
| `cases.chase_priority` | enum | `normal` | Priority of a chase |

## Alerts

How far ahead the register looks, and what counts as pressing.

Owned by `alerts`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alerts.horizon_days` | integer | `90` | The default window on the alerts page and the dashboard. |
| `alerts.urgent_days` | integer | `14` | Anything due inside this window is counted as pressing rather than upcoming. |
| `alerts.unbilled_days` | enum | `90` | Matters that finished without a fee, an invoice or an agreed fee. Older than this is treated as history rather than a missed payment — the register holds an archive of matters already dealt with, and without a window this would name every one of them. Widen it as the fees on file get more complete. |
| `alerts.unbilled_grace_days` | integer | `14` | How long after a matter finishes before it is worth mentioning. A matter decided yesterday has not been forgotten, and being nagged on the day is how a page stops being read. |
| `alerts.mail_quiet_days` | integer | `3` | The register checks the mailbox every few minutes. If the checking is working but nothing has come in for this many days, something before it is probably broken — forwarding, or the domain’s mail records. Set to the longest quiet spell that would not worry you. |
| `alerts.certificate_notice_days` | integer | `30` | A police certificate, medical or x-ray inside this window counts as pressing rather than upcoming. Replacing one takes weeks — a police certificate from overseas can take longer than that — so the warning has to come while there is still time to act on it. |
| `alerts.ack_days` | integer | `14` | A lodged matter with no INZ application number recorded after this long is listed under “Not acknowledged”. Either the acknowledgement never came, or it came and nobody wrote the number down — and both are worth knowing before you need to quote it. |
| `alerts.quiet_days` | integer | `10` | An open matter with no note, no status change and no task activity for this long is listed under “Gone quiet”. Nothing is due on it — that is the point. Matters are rarely lost to a missed deadline; they are lost to nobody looking. |

## Quotes

How quotes are put together and how long they stand.

Owned by `quotes`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quotes.email_subject` | string | `Fee quote {quote_ref} — {matter}` | Placeholders in braces are filled in: {quote_ref}, {matter}, {client_name}, {practice_name}. Anything else in braces prints as you typed it, so a misspelling shows up on the preview screen rather than reaching the client. |
| `quotes.email_body` | text | `Dear {client_name},

Thank you for your enquiry and for discussing your matter with us.

As discussed, I am pleased to provide you with our **fee quotation{and_letter}** for the proposed work.

{total}

{link_block}

{terms}

Please note that **acceptance of the quotation does not constitute a guarantee that any visa, immigration application or other outcome will be successful**. Immigration decisions are made by Immigration New Zealand in accordance with the applicable legislation, immigration instructions and its decision-making powers.

{closing_date} {capacity}

{how_to_accept}

If you have any questions about the quotation, scope of work or terms of engagement, please contact us before accepting it. We will be happy to clarify any aspect of the proposed engagement.

Kind regards,
{signature}` | The covering letter sent with every quotation. Placeholders in braces are filled in from the quotation — {client_name}, {total}, {link_block}, {terms}, {closing_date}, {capacity}, {how_to_accept}, {signature} and others; the Email page lists them all. You still see and can edit every letter before it goes, and the Preview screen shows exactly what the client will read. |
| `quotes.validity_days` | integer | `7` | Counted inclusive of the day it is issued — issued on the 28th, seven days means it is good through the 3rd. The quote shows the date, never a number of days, so the client does not have to work it out. |
| `quotes.capacity_note` | text | `This quote is subject to our capacity to accept the work at the time you accept it.` | Printed on every quote beneath the total. Leave blank to omit it. |
| `quotes.payment_terms` | text | `Fees are payable in advance into the practice trust account. Disbursements are payable as they fall due.` | Printed on every quote. Leave blank to omit it. |
| `quotes.default_unit_label` | string | `item` | What one of something is called when a line does not say otherwise. |
| `quotes.template_lines` | text | _blank_ | One per line, as kind \| Description \| GST — for example “professional \| Professional time \| exclusive” or “disbursement \| INZ application fee \| inclusive”. Kind is professional, disbursement or third_party. Every line arrives with no amount. Easiest set by opening a quotation you are happy with and pressing “Use as the template”. |
| `quotes.template_stages` | text | _blank_ | One per line, as Label \| What it is for and when it falls due \| GST. Every stage arrives with no amount. Leave both boxes empty and new quotations start blank, as they always did. |

## Letter of engagement

The words every letter of engagement says. The parties, the work and the fees are not here — they are on the quotation the letter goes out with, and the letter refers to it rather than repeating it. The clauses in the middle of the letter are edited separately, under Quotes → Letter clauses, because there can be any number of them and some belong only on certain kinds of matter.

Owned by `quotes`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `engagement.subject` | string | `Letter of Engagement for Legal Services` | Printed as the RE: line under the client’s address. |
| `engagement.opening` | text | _blank_ | The paragraphs before the clauses — that you are pleased to act, who has overall responsibility for the matter, who the client deals with day to day, and how they accept. Blank lines separate paragraphs. Nothing is supplied: this is your wording, not the register’s. |
| `engagement.terms_title` | string | `Short Form Terms of Engagement` | Printed across the page where the covering letter ends and the terms begin. Leave blank and no dividing heading is printed. |
| `engagement.terms_subtitle` | string | `Immigration Legal Services` | Ignored when the heading above is blank. |
| `engagement.scope_heading` | string | `Scope of the Retainer` | Ignored when there is no wording below. |
| `engagement.scope_terms` | text | _blank_ | Printed immediately under the block that points at the quotation. Blank lines separate paragraphs; **two asterisks** around a phrase print it in bold. Nothing is supplied: this is your wording, not the register’s. |
| `engagement.addendum_heading` | string | `Addendum 1 — Information for Clients` | Ignored when there is no wording below. |
| `engagement.addendum` | text | _blank_ | Printed after the signature, starting a new page. For the information the Rules of Conduct and Client Care require a client to be given. Blank lines separate paragraphs; a line beginning “- ” prints as a bullet; **two asterisks** around a phrase print it in bold. |
| `engagement.admin_team_heading` | string | `Day-to-Day Administrative Team Contact` | The heading of the section. Ignored when no people are listed below. |
| `engagement.admin_team_intro` | string | `The designated administrative (non-legal) contacts for this engagement are:` | Printed above the list. |
| `engagement.admin_team` | text | _blank_ | One person per line, written however you would write it — a name on its own, or a name with a mobile and an email after it. Each line is printed on the letter exactly as you type it here. Leave the box empty and the section is not printed. |
| `engagement.admin_team_also` | string | `or any other person nominated by them` | Printed as the last item of the list. Leave blank to name only the people above. |
| `engagement.acknowledgements` | text | _blank_ | One per line, printed as a numbered list above the signature. Numbering you paste in (“1.”, “2)”, a bullet) is taken off, so the list is not numbered twice. Put **two asterisks** around a phrase to print it in bold. Leave blank to print no list at all. |
| `engagement.acknowledgements_heading` | string | `What you confirm by accepting` | The heading above the numbered list. Ignored when the list is empty. |
| `engagement.acknowledgements_intro` | string | `By accepting these terms, the client confirms that they:` | Ignored when the list above is empty. |
| `engagement.closing` | text | _blank_ | The paragraphs after the clauses and before the signature. |
| `engagement.signature_name` | string | _blank_ | Left blank, the practice’s own name from Practice details is used. |
| `engagement.signature_title` | string | _blank_ | For example Barrister, or Licensed Immigration Adviser. |

## Inbound channels

What happens to a message the moment it arrives. Which senders are trusted is set by allow-list secrets, not here — a message from anyone else always waits for triage, whatever these say.

Owned by `inbox`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ingest.auto_create_inquiries` | boolean | `false` | Off by default: everything that arrives waits in the inbox until somebody acts on it, so there is one place to look. Turn this on and mail from an allow-listed sender becomes an inquiry the moment it lands, without passing through the inbox. |

## Knowledge base

What the knowledge base holds, and when it reminds you. Kinds take one per line, written as “key \| Label”. The key is what is stored and cannot contain spaces; renaming a label is free, but changing a key leaves existing articles on the old one.

Owned by `knowledge`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kb.kinds` | text | `visa_pack \| Visa pack
circular \| Internal circular
legal \| Legal material
announcement \| Announcement
instructions \| Immigration instructions
policy \| Policy and procedure
template \| Template or precedent
guide \| How-to guide
practice_note \| General practice note` | Kinds of article |
| `kb.followups_enabled` | boolean | `true` | When an article carries a date that matters, raise a task against it. |
| `kb.followup_lead_days` | integer | `7` | 7 gives you a week’s warning. 0 raises the task on the day itself. Changing this corrects every existing follow-up overnight. |
| `kb.followup_priority` | enum | `normal` | Priority of those tasks |
| `kb.review_after_months` | integer | `12` | Used to fill in the review date when an article is created. 0 leaves it blank. |

## Nightly backup

A copy of the whole register, written every night without anybody pressing anything.

Owned by `admin`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backup.nightly` | boolean | `1` | On unless you have a reason. A register with this off has only the copy Cloudflare keeps, which is not one you hold. |
| `backup.keep` | integer | `30` | Older ones are removed. The newest is never removed, whatever this says. |

## Practice caseload

For a register set up so people can try it and learn. Leave this alone on a register holding real files.

Owned by `admin`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `testdata.auto_reset_days` | integer | `0` | Zero means never, which is what a register holding real files wants. Anything else deletes every record marked as test data on that schedule. |
